# Source-comparison report

The complete brief/source package, complete draft, and quotation guidance were read. Target language is en_US. All quotations are English; no translation review is applicable. This report assesses source support, including titles, attribution, qualifications, implications, and the link destination. It does not conduct an editorial or mechanical review.

## Supporting source passages

The identifiers below denote exact supplied passages. Each accounting row cites the passage that supports its proposition and rules out its precise negation. Assertions about Lind's speech are tested as assertions about her reported speech, not as independently verified facts about the world.

- S1: “The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems. The customer, Elm Quay Housing, should remain the acting party.”
- S2: “The optional next step is the supplied implementation checklist at https://example.invalid/svale/checklist; it is a document to read, not a consultation booking or a product trial.”
- S3: “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”
- S4: “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”
- S5: “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.”
- S6: “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”
- S7: “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair. No comparison with another supplier is available.”
- S8: “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”
- S9: “Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.”
- S10: “The trial lasted eight weeks.”
- S11: “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered. It excludes emergencies and work ordered before the trial.”
- S12: “Median time from report to assignment was two working days during the trial and three in the preceding eight-week period.”
- S13: “The periods had different workloads, and the note explicitly does not attribute the difference to the software.”
- S14: “There are no cost, resident-satisfaction or completion-time measurements.”
- S15: “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”
- S16: “We wanted the evening shift to see what the morning shift had already done. The categories were ours; Svale helped us put them into the log.”
- S17: “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”
- S18: “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”
- S19: “Lind did not recommend Svale to every housing company. Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment. It is not an inference from the figures.”
- S20: “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs.”
- S21: “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.”
- S22: “All interviews occurred by email, and no physical scene, emotion or remembered dialogue is provided.”

## Complete claim accounting

“Supported” means the cited supplied statement rules out the listed negation when the proposition is read with its original scope. Repeated claims receive separate rows when they occur in another draft passage. Ellipses in the passage column abbreviate the location only; the standalone proposition column retains the applicable qualifications.

## Source-support findings

No unsupported or altered claim was found. Consequently, no source-compatible counterexample is needed for an unsupported proposition, and no repair is proposed.

The title's qualitative “finds value” is grounded in Lind's direct “helps us” assessment and immediately specified in the introduction. It makes no numerical, cost, satisfaction, completion-speed, or assignment-speed benefit claim. The measured comparison retains both the different workloads and the note's refusal to attribute the difference to software. The customer remains the actor in the choice, category design, trial, and expansion decision. The count carries both exclusions without an unsupported size characterization. The qualified endorsement remains qualified throughout its paraphrases and quotation.

All three quotations match the supplied wording, with only the conventional terminal punctuation adjustment before the first quotation's attribution. Their attribution to an email interview is supported. No physical scene, remembered dialogue, emotion, comparative supplier performance, or customer helplessness is introduced. The second quotation supplies the comparative category-preparation experience; the third supplies the specific extra-week reservation. No quotation creates an unsupplied experience to fill the format.

## Translation findings

None: source and draft are English. The quotations preserve wording, meaning, stance, certainty, and distinctive voice. “Apartments” for narrative “flats” is a meaning-preserving en_US locale choice and is outside quoted speech.

Completion status: complete. Unresolved findings: none.
